items.title: Nondimensionalisation of the one-dimensional stationary equation and of the WKB exponent
items.statement:
Let $\ell>0$ and $E_\star>0$ be real reference scales, let $m>0$ and
$\hbar>0$ be real, and define
$$h:=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}}>0 .$$
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let
$W\in C^2(I;\mathbb R)$, let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and let $u:I\to\mathbb C$
be a function. Then:

(a) $u$ is of class $C^2$ on $I$ and satisfies
$$u''(\xi)=\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^2}\,u(\xi)\qquad(\xi\in I)$$
if and only if the function $\psi:\ell I\to\mathbb C$, $\psi(x):=u(x/\ell)$,
is of class $C^2$ on the open interval $\ell I=\{\ell\xi:\xi\in I\}$ and
satisfies
$$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,\psi''(x)+E_\star W(x/\ell)\,\psi(x)=E_\star\lambda\,\psi(x) \qquad(x\in\ell I);$$

(b) if $a<b$ are points of $I$, then each of the following identities holds
under its indicated strict-sign hypothesis:

(i) if $W(\xi)-\lambda>0$ for every $\xi\in[a,b]$, then
$$\frac1h\int_a^b\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi =\frac1\hbar\int_{\ell a}^{\ell b}\sqrt{2m\bigl(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda\bigr)}\,dx ;$$

(ii) if $\lambda-W(\xi)>0$ for every $\xi\in[a,b]$, then
$$\frac1h\int_a^b\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}\,d\xi =\frac1\hbar\int_{\ell a}^{\ell b}\sqrt{2m\bigl(E_\star\lambda-E_\star W(x/\ell)\bigr)}\,dx .$$

All square roots here are the nonnegative real square roots of strictly
positive numbers. Part (i) is the forbidden-region exponent identity; part
(ii) is the allowed-region phase identity.

The identities are statements about the displayed functions and integrals
only. The number $h$ is dimensionless because $\hbar$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$
and $\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}$ is in $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,s}$;
no physical interpretation, no approximation and no error estimate is
asserted here.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 11.6 printed pages 253-254 (PDF pages 261-262): the WKBJ equation d^2 psi/dx^2 = -k^2 psi with k^2 = 2m(E-V)/hbar^2 and the phase phi(x) = int k dx

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 5.4 'WKB Approximation' printed and PDF pages 70-72 (the one-dimensional WKB solution with the local wavenumber and the phase integral, in the same reduced equation)

items.title: Finite-rank gapped spectral cluster under a bounded perturbation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and $H_0=H_0^*$ a self-adjoint operator on its exact dense domain $D=D(H_0)$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Let $E\in\mathbb R$ be an isolated eigenvalue with $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_0)\setminus\{E\})\ge g>0$, and let its orthogonal spectral projection $P_0=E_{H_0}(\{E\})$ have finite rank $r\ge1$. The PVM and gap calculus are those of [[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-arbitrary-hilbert-spectral-calculus]]. Let $V=V^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $v=\|V\|\ge0$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]). Put $H_\lambda=H_0+\lambda V$ on $D$, and define
$$\Omega_v=\begin{cases}\{\lambda\in\mathbb C:|\lambda|<g/(2v)\},&v>0,\\\mathbb C,&v=0.\end{cases}$$
For $\lambda\in\Omega_v$ write $q_\lambda=2|\lambda|v/g<1$, $\Gamma=\{z:|z-E|=g/2\}$ oriented counterclockwise, and $\Delta=\{z:|z-E|<g/2\}$.

**(a) Resolvent and exact domain.** $H_\lambda$ is closed and densely defined on $D$. Every $z\in\Gamma$ is a resolvent point, with the convention $R_\lambda(z)=(z-H_\lambda)^{-1}:H\to D$ of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], and
$$R_\lambda(z)=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(\lambda VR_0(z))^k,\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)\|\le\frac{2/g}{1-q_\lambda},\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)-R_0(z)\|\le\frac2g\frac{q_\lambda}{1-q_\lambda}.$$
The series converges in operator norm uniformly on $\Gamma$ and locally uniformly in $\lambda\in\Omega_v$.

**(b) Finite-rank holomorphic cluster.** The norm contour integral
$$P_\lambda=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma R_\lambda(z)\,dz$$
is a bounded idempotent of rank exactly $r$ throughout $\Omega_v$, with $P_{\lambda=0}=P_0$ and $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le q_\lambda/(1-q_\lambda)$. It is holomorphic in operator norm. Its range $M_\lambda=P_\lambda H$ lies in $D$ and is invariant under $H_\lambda$, and $P_\lambda H_\lambda=H_\lambda P_\lambda$ on $D$. Both $H_\lambda P_\lambda\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $P_\lambda:H\to(D,\|x\|+\|H_0x\|)$ are holomorphic in their respective operator norms.

**(c) Exactly the enclosed spectrum.** Let $A_\lambda=H_\lambda|_{M_\lambda}:M_\lambda\to M_\lambda$. Then
$$\sigma(H_\lambda)\cap\Delta=\sigma(A_\lambda)\subset\Delta.$$
This is a nonempty finite set of at most $r$ eigenvalues. The restriction of $w-H_\lambda$ to $\ker P_\lambda$ has a bounded two-sided inverse on its exact domain $D\cap\ker P_\lambda$ for every $w\in\Delta$. Consequently all generalized eigenvectors at an enclosed eigenvalue belong to $M_\lambda$; their eigenspaces and generalized eigenspaces are those of this finite-dimensional restriction.

**(d) Real coupling and zero perturbation.** For real $\lambda$, $H_\lambda$ is self-adjoint on $D$. For real $\lambda\in\Omega_v$, $P_\lambda=E_{H_\lambda}((E-g/2,E+g/2))$ is the orthogonal projection on the entire enclosed spectral cluster ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). If $v=0$, then $V=0$, $H_\lambda=H_0$ and $P_\lambda=P_0$ for every complex coupling, with $A_\lambda=E I_{M_0}$ and enclosed spectrum $\{E\}$.

No separability or arbitrary-index Axiom of Choice is assumed. The claim supplies a cluster and its finite restriction; for $r>1$ it supplies no ordering or individually holomorphic scalar eigenvalue branches.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.6: contour perturbation; finite-rank extension proved locally here

items.title: The declared variational trial reading: assigned energy observable, form domain, trial value, bottom and gap
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the
state reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the sharp
observable reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of
the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Assigned energy observable.** As an additional model assumption of the
pair, fix a self-adjoint operator $H:D(H)\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$ on
the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ and **declare** the pair
$(H,\mathrm J)$ to be the system's sharp energy observable in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a); this
identification of the operator with the energy of the system is an assumption
of the model, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. Assume $H$ is **bounded
below**: there is a real $c$ with $\langle Hu,u\rangle\ge c\|u\|^{2}$ for every
$u\in D(H)$. The spectrum $\sigma(H)$ is the set of the cited spectral
theorem, and the **model bottom** is
$$E_{0}:=\inf\sigma(H)\in[c,+\infty),$$
read in joules. An assignment of a concrete material system to the pair
$(H,\mathfrak H)$ is a tested identification in the sense of the preparation
and apparatus discipline P7 and is not made here.

**(c) Form domain and trial value.** Let $Q(H):=D\bigl((H-cI)^{1/2}\bigr)$ and
$q_{H}$ be the form domain and the closed semibounded form of
[[lem-spectral-form-domain-and-core-of-a-semibounded-operator]] for the lower
bound $c$ of clause (b), with
$$q_{H}[u]=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{u}(\lambda)\qquad(u\in Q(H)),$$
$E$ the projection-valued measure of $H$ and $E_{u}(B)=\langle E(B)u,u\rangle$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). The definition uses the facts, proved by
that lemma, that $q_H$ does not depend on the choice of the lower bound $c$, that
$D(H)$ is dense in $Q(H)$, and that $q_{H}[u]=\langle Hu,u\rangle$ for
$u\in D(H)$. A **trial vector** of the model is a vector $u\in Q(H)$ with
$\|u\|=1$; its **trial value** is $q_{H}[u]$, read in joules. For a trial
vector that lies in $D(H)$, the trial value is the mean energy of the pure
preparation $[u]$ under the observable $(H,\mathrm J)$ in the moment reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]]; for a general trial vector in
$Q(H)\setminus D(H)$ the trial value is the form value and is not asserted to
be the mean of any outcome law.

**(d) Bottom gap and discrete ladder.** If the bottom is an isolated spectral
value, declare a **gap** to be a real $g>0$ with
$$\sigma(H)\cap(E_{0},E_{0}+g)=\varnothing,$$
and put $P:=E(\{E_{0}\})$ for the bottom spectral projection. The **discrete
spectrum below the essential spectrum** is the part of
$\sigma_{\mathrm d}(H)$ of
[[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]] below
$\Lambda:=\inf\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H)$, listed with multiplicity in
nondecreasing order as $E_{1}\le E_{2}\le\cdots$, with the convention
$E_{n}:=\Lambda$ once the list is exhausted, $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$. The
definition asserts neither that $E_{0}$ is an eigenvalue, nor that any
eigenvector exists, nor that $E_{0}=E_{1}$.

**(e) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) are a reading of the framework's state,
observable and dynamics postulates together with the declared operator $H$;
they assert nothing about whether a preparation attains the trial value, about
the behaviour of any preparation under time evolution beyond P4, about
equilibration, environmental coupling, measurement or apparatus, and about any
measured energy. All spectral statements are statements about the declared
operator.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.2 printed page 212 (PDF page 220): Rayleigh's theorem, the upper bound <H> >= E0 for any state and the variational principle for a trial wavefunction

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 1 'Wave Mechanics', Section 5 printed pages 19-21 (PDF pages 18-20): the trial-wavefunction upper bound E_gs <= <H>_psi (5.13) and the unnormalised functional F[psi] (5.20)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.3 printed pages 117-119 (PDF pages 129-131): the min-max theorem below the essential spectrum and the form-domain reading of the trial family

items.physical_scope: The variational trial reading of a declared system of the framework: a self-adjoint assigned energy observable H bounded below, its form domain Q(H) and form q_H supplied by the cited spectral-form mathematics, the model bottom E(0) = inf sigma(H), an isolated bottom with a declared gap g and its spectral projection, the discrete eigenvalue ladder below the essential spectrum, and the declared vocabulary of trial vector and trial value. The definition asserts nothing about whether the bottom is attained, about any eigenvector, about any laboratory realization or identification, and about any measurement, apparatus or sampling model.

items.title: The declared perturbed-family model: bounded self-adjoint perturbation, isolated gapped label and followed spectral label
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the
state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical
suppliers.

**(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair,
fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$
on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the
unperturbed sharp energy observable,
fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with
$$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless:
$\lambda V$ is read in joules). Declare the **perturbed family**
$$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$
to be the model's sharp energy observable at coupling $\lambda$. Since $V$ is
$H_{0}$-bounded with $H_{0}$-bound $0\le a<1$ (the bound inequality holds with
$a=0$ and $b=v$), the Kato-Rellich theorem applies and $H(\lambda)$ is
self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ for every real $\lambda$
([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
This self-adjointness is a supplied theorem about the declared operators; the
reading of the family as the system's energy is the model assumption.

**(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$
of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$
and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The
definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers:

(i) for real $\lambda$ with $2|\lambda|v/g<1$, the **followed spectral cluster** is the spectrum of $H(\lambda)$ inside $|z-E|<g/2$, and
$$P_\lambda:=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z-E|=g/2}(z-H(\lambda))^{-1}\,dz$$
(counterclockwise) is its rank-$r$ orthogonal spectral projection, by [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]]. The cluster is a nonempty finite set and is exactly the spectrum of the restriction to $P_\lambda\mathfrak H$. In the simple case $r=1$ only, write $E_\lambda$ for its unique spectral value; this scalar is the followed perturbed label of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] and is analytic on the valid coupling disk. For $r>1$ no unique scalar label, branch ordering or individual scalar holomorphy is presumed. At $\lambda=0$ the cluster is $\{E\}$ and its projection is $P_0$. If $v=0$, these data are constant for all real couplings, with no radius involving division by $v$.

(ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift
data (joules per unit coupling);

(iii) the **complementary reduced inverse**
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$
is a bounded operator with the displayed exact complementary-domain inverse. For every finite multiplicity $r\ge1$, including $v=0$, its existence follows by applying part (c) of [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]] at coupling $\lambda=0$ and $w=E$: since the cluster projection is then $P_0$, the restriction of $E-H_0$ to $D(H_0)\cap Q_0\mathfrak H$ has a bounded two-sided inverse $R_Q(E):Q_0\mathfrak H\to D(H_0)\cap Q_0\mathfrak H$, and $S=-\iota_{Q_0}R_Q(E)Q_0$. For $r=1$ the same operator is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]. Its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint
operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition
asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no
statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any
eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no
measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the
labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1 printed pages 203-211 (PDF pages 211-219): time-independent perturbation theory, the first- and second-order energy shifts, the quadratic Stark effect and the degenerate-subspace diagonalisation of the perturbation (9.4)-(9.18)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 6 printed pages 133-159 (PDF pages 145-171): relatively bounded operators, the Kato-Rellich theorem (Theorem 6.4) and norm resolvent convergence for bounded perturbations

items.physical_scope: The perturbed-family model of a declared system of the framework: a self-adjoint unperturbed energy observable H0, a bounded self-adjoint perturbation V with norm v, the real coupling lambda and the family H(lambda) = H0 + lambda V declared as the model's energy observable at coupling lambda, together with a fixed isolated eigenvalue E of H0 of finite multiplicity with gap g, its spectral projection, the first-order operator P0VP0 on the eigenspace, and the followed perturbed spectral label supplied by the contour construction. The definition asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no ramping protocol, no occupation of any branch by a preparation, no measurement and no laboratory identification; all statements are about the declared operator family.

items.title: The declared WKB regime model: nondimensionalised line equation, turning points, phase integrals and the declared barrier transmission reading
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data and line model.** Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), the
state and observable readings cited there, and the declared effective
one-dimensional line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with a mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and units from
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a real potential
$$V\in C_c^{5}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$$
(five times continuously differentiable with compact support); it is real,
bounded and measurable, so the line model's assigned energy operator $H_{V}$
of its clause (c) is defined with domain $D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb
C)$, acts by $H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}f+Vf$, and its stationary
equation at energy $E$ reads
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$$
for classically $C^{2}$ solutions.

**(b) Reference scales and nondimensionalisation.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair fix a **reference length** $\ell>0$ (metres) and a
**reference energy** $E_\star>0$ (joules), and put
$$W(\xi):=\frac{V(\ell\xi)}{E_\star},\qquad \lambda:=\frac{E}{E_\star},\qquad h:=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}} .$$
Then $W\in C_c^{5}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ is dimensionless with support scaled by
$\ell$, and $h>0$ is dimensionless. By
[[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] the physical
stationary equation of clause (a) at energy $E$ is equivalent, under
$x=\ell\xi$, $\psi(\ell\xi)=u(\xi)$, to the **dimensionless WKB equation**
$$u''(\xi)=\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^{2}}\,u(\xi),\qquad \xi\in I,$$
on every interval $I$. The exact transfer of the square-root action integrals
over a subinterval $[x_a,x_b]=\ell[a,b]$ is, when the indicated strict sign
holds throughout $[a,b]$,
$$\frac1\hbar\int_{x_a}^{x_b}\sqrt{2m(V(x)-E)}\,dx=\frac1h\int_a^b\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi\quad\text{if }W-\lambda>0,$$
$$\frac1\hbar\int_{x_a}^{x_b}\sqrt{2m(E-V(x))}\,dx=\frac1h\int_a^b\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}\,d\xi\quad\text{if }\lambda-W>0;$$
these are respectively clauses (b)(i) and (b)(ii) of
[[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]]. The pair calls
$h$ the model's **semiclassical parameter** and calls
$h\ll1$ the **semiclassical regime**; the physical content of the regime is
$\hbar\ll\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}$, and every statement of the page's theorems is
an exact statement about the family indexed by $h$, with the error bounds
stated at each $h$. For the mathematical small-$h$ limit, hold the dimensionless profile $W$ and energy $\lambda$ fixed and vary the parameter in $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^2$. A corresponding physical family with fixed $m,E_\star,\hbar$ is obtained by taking $\ell_h=\hbar/(h\sqrt{2mE_\star})$ and $V_h(x)=E_\star W(x/\ell_h)$, with $E=E_\star\lambda$; the physical width then changes, while the natural action constant does not. A single originally chosen $V,\ell,E_\star$ supplies one member of this family.

**(c) Turning points, regions and phase.** For the data $(W,\lambda)$ put
$$\tau:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R: W(\xi)=\lambda\}$$
for the set of **turning points**. A point $\xi_{0}\in\tau$ is **simple** when
$W'(\xi_{0})\ne0$. An open interval $J$ is an **allowed interval** when
$W(\xi)-\lambda<0$ on $J$ (the dimensionless kinetic energy $-(W-\lambda)$ is
positive there), a **forbidden interval** when $W(\xi)-\lambda>0$ on
$J$. On an allowed interval the model uses the local wavenumber
$$p(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0$$
and the WKB phase $\theta(\xi):=\int_{\xi_{\mathrm{ref}}}^{\xi}p(s)\,ds$ with a
declared base point; on a forbidden interval the model uses
$\kappa(\xi):=\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}>0$. The **WKB exponent** of a forbidden
interval $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$ is
$$S:=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi =\frac{h}{\hbar}\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V(x)-E)}\,dx,$$
equivalently $S/h$ is the physical action in units of $\hbar$. For a
barrier whose endpoints are simple turning points, the strict-sign hypothesis
of clause (b)(i) fails at those endpoints; apply that clause on
$[\xi_a+\delta,\xi_b-\delta]$ and let $\delta\downarrow0$. Both integrands
extend continuously with value zero at the endpoints, so the omitted endpoint
integrals tend to zero. The
three declared regime hypotheses used by the page are:

(W1) **Allowed-interval regularity**: $W\in C^{2}$ on a neighbourhood of
$[a,b]$ and $\lambda-W\ge\delta>0$ on $[a,b]$ for some $\delta>0$ (no turning
point in the interval; the interval is allowed);

(W2) **Separated simple turning points**: $W-\lambda$ has exactly two zeros
$\xi_{a}<\xi_{b}$ in $\mathbb R$, both simple, is positive on
$(\xi_{a},\xi_{b})$ and negative on the complement of $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$
(equivalently the physical barrier $V-E$ has exactly two simple zeros
surrounding a forbidden region and is negative outside);

(W3) **Single simple turning point**: on an interval $[\xi_{0}-r,\xi_{0}+s]$
the equation $W-\lambda$ has the single zero $\xi_{0}$, it is simple, and
$W-\lambda<0$ on one side and $>0$ on the other.

**(d) Declared barrier transmission reading.** Under (W2), $\lambda>0$ because $W=0$ outside its compact support. Choose $R>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}W\subset(-R,R)$ and put $p_\infty:=\sqrt\lambda$. The declared scattering solution is the exact $C^2$ solution of the dimensionless equation with boundary conditions
$$u_h(\xi)=p_\infty^{-1/2}\bigl(e^{ip_\infty\xi/h}+r(h)e^{-ip_\infty\xi/h}\bigr)\quad(\xi\le-R),\qquad u_h(\xi)=p_\infty^{-1/2}t(h)e^{ip_\infty\xi/h}\quad(\xi\ge R).$$
Thus there is one incoming wave from the left and none from the right. These data determine unique amplitudes by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-two-turn-barrier-tunnelling-error]], instantiated with its mass parameter $1/2$, potential $W$ and energy $\lambda$. Define the reference current $J_h(u):=h\operatorname{Im}(\overline u\,u')$: the normalized exterior waves have currents $\pm1$. The transmission coefficient is $T(h):=|t(h)|^2$, the ratio of transmitted to incoming reference current. The physical line-model current is a positive common multiple of $J_h$ under clause (b), so its ratio is also $T(h)$. Airy/WKB matching computes this exact boundary-defined quantity; it does not define an additional approximate scattering solution. No detector, wave packet, scattering experiment or measured count is asserted, and this clause does not by itself assert an asymptotic formula for $T(h)$.

**(e) Scope.** The model concerns a declared spinless massive particle in the
declared one-dimensional line model with a compactly supported $C^{5}$
potential, at a fixed energy, in the nondimensionalised family of clause (b).
It asserts nothing about two- or three-dimensional scattering, about singular
or non-smooth potentials, about wave packets, detectors or measurements, and
about any laboratory realization of the line model, the potential $V$ or the
energy $E$.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 11.6 printed pages 253-254 (PDF pages 261-262): the WKBJ equation with k^2 = 2m(E-V)/hbar^2, the phase phi = int k dx, the slowly varying condition and the flux-conserving WKBJ wavefunction

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Sections 5.4-5.6 printed and PDF pages 70-75: 5.4 WKB Approximation pp. 70-72, 5.5 Cold Emission pp. 72-73, 5.6 Alpha Decay pp. 73-75 (WKB wavefunctions in allowed and forbidden regions, turning points and barrier transmission)

items.title: Static finite-level electric-dipole coupling: compressed dipole of the declared two-body Coulomb model in a uniform field
items.statement:
Adopt as a physical assumption of the pair, additional to P1, P2 and P4 and
valid only for the declared finite-level model of this clause, the following
static electric-dipole coupling. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the
Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(i) Declared charged pair and relative coordinate.** Take the declared
two-body Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d): two
distinguishable spinless particles with mass parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ and
opposite charges $-q$ and $+q$, $q>0$ (coulombs), with the relative coordinate
$r=x_{1}-x_{2}$ and the centre-of-mass/relative unitary
$U_{\Phi}$. Work in the relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb
R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of that reading, with Coulomb mass parameter $m=\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, and with units as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(ii) Dipole operator.** Let $Q_{j}$, $j=1,2,3$, be the coordinate
multiplication operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with maximal
domains $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi:\xi_{j}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clause (a); they are
self-adjoint and proper densely defined. The model's **dipole operator** is
the triple
$$D_{j}:=-q\,Q_{j}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
because the dipole of charges $-q$ at $x_{1}$ and $+q$ at $x_{2}$ is
$-qx_{1}+qx_{2}=-qr$: it points from the negative to the positive charge,
opposite to the declared relative coordinate $r=x_{1}-x_{2}$. Each $D_{j}$ is
self-adjoint on $D(Q_{j})$ and has unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$. This is the dipole of
the declared pair in its relative-coordinate reading; no multipole expansion,
no field equation and no coupling to the centre-of-mass motion is assumed.

**(iii) Finite-level truncation.** Fix, as part of the model specification, a
**declared finite-dimensional subspace** $W\subseteq D(H_\kappa)\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap
D(Q_{3})$ of the relative-coordinate space with $D(H_\kappa)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and $\dim W=d<\infty$, together
with an orthonormal basis of $W$. The model declares the **compressed dipole
matrix** on $W$,
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W},$$
where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$ and the restriction to
$W$ is read in the declared orthonormal basis; $D^{W}_{j}$ is the finite
Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix of the dipole component, with unit
$\mathrm{C\,m}$, and it is bounded with norm at most $\sup_{\psi\in
W,\|\psi\|=1}\|D_{j}\psi\|$. The truncation and the basis are model
assumptions: they are not derived from the Coulomb model, and they replace
the unbounded operator $D_{j}$ by its compression throughout this pair.

**(iv) Static uniform field and interaction operator.** The external datum is
a **uniform static electric field value** $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\in\mathbb
R^{3}$, read in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$; it is prescribed, and no Maxwell
equation, source model, propagation or back-reaction is assumed. The
**finite-level static Stark model** is the finite-dimensional operator on $W$
$$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext}):=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W} -\sum_{j=1}^{3}E_{{\rm ext},j}\,D^{W}_{j},$$
where the energy-domain condition of (iii) makes the compression defined,
and $H_{\kappa}=C_{\mu}$ is the one-centre Coulomb energy operator with
mass parameter $m=\mu$ of the declared model, read on the relative-coordinate
factor through the angular/radial
identification used by the pair. The interaction term has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm J$ and is bounded Hermitian on $W$, so
$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext})$ is a bounded Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix and
the Kato-Rellich and perturbation statements of the pair apply to it with a
bounded perturbation; this identification of the matrix with the model's
energy on the truncated subspace is a model assumption.

**(v) Scope and explicit exclusion.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted model
assumptions. They assert nothing about a laboratory atom, field or apparatus;
no measured Stark shift is claimed; no transition, absorption or emission
rate is defined; and no time dependence of the field is assumed. In
particular the postulate deliberately does **not** treat the uncompressed
linear potential $-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D$ as a bounded
perturbation of $H_{\kappa}$. For $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\ne0$, define this
composite interaction to be the maximal multiplication operator
$$M_{\mathbf E}\psi(\mathbf r):=q\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf r\,\psi(\mathbf r),\qquad D(M_{\mathbf E}):=\{\psi\in L^2:(\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf r)\psi\in L^2\};$$
it agrees with $-\sum_jE_{{\rm ext},j}D_j$ on the common domain
$\bigcap_jD(D_j)$ and is unbounded because its real multiplier is
unbounded. The common operator domain $D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(M_{\mathbf E})$ contains
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Its lack of a lower bound can be demonstrated
without assuming a full energy-form domain: let $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\ne0$,
$\widehat e=\mathbf E_{\rm ext}/|\mathbf E_{\rm ext}|$, choose a fixed
support radius $\rho>0$ in metres and normalized
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(B(0,\rho);\mathbb C)$, and for each length $R>\rho$ put
$$\psi_R(\mathbf r):=\varphi(\mathbf r+R\widehat e).$$
Then $\psi_R\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\subset
D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(M_{\mathbf E})\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^3D(Q_j)$ and
$\|\psi_R\|_2=1$. On this common test domain define the quadratic
expectation
$$\mathcal Q_{\mathbf E_{\rm ext}}[\psi]:=\langle H_{\kappa}\psi,\psi\rangle+\langle M_{\mathbf E}\psi,\psi\rangle.$$
With $\mathbf s=\mathbf r+R\widehat e$, the Coulomb action and the
translation-invariant kinetic expectation give
$$\mathcal Q_{\mathbf E_{\rm ext}}[\psi_R]=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mu}\int|\nabla\varphi(\mathbf s)|^2d\mathbf s-\kappa\int\frac{|\varphi(\mathbf s)|^2}{|\mathbf s-R\widehat e|}d\mathbf s+q\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\int\mathbf s|\varphi(\mathbf s)|^2d\mathbf s-qR|\mathbf E_{\rm ext}|.$$
Here $-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D=q\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf r$
because $\mathbf D=-q\mathbf r$ in the relative-coordinate convention.
For $R>\rho$, the Coulomb integral is finite and at most $1/(R-\rho)$,
the kinetic term is constant, and the other field term apart from
$-qR|\mathbf E_{\rm ext}|$ is independent of $R$. Therefore
$\mathcal Q_{\mathbf E_{\rm ext}}[\psi_R]\to-\infty$ as $R\to\infty$.
This proves unboundedness below of the displayed quadratic expectation on
the common test domain, so no quadratic form bounded below there can agree
with these values; no claim is made about a particular closed-form domain.
The uncompressed static-field
model is outside the scope of every statement of this pair. Only the
compressed finite-level operator of clause (iv) is used.

items.title: Variational trial bounds, gap-overlap control and the min-max characterisation of the declared model's discrete eigenvalues
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared variational trial model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-variational-trial-model]]: a declared
system with self-adjoint assigned energy observable $H$ on $\mathfrak H$,
bounded below by a real $c$, with model bottom $E_{0}=\inf\sigma(H)$, form
domain $Q(H)$, form $q_{H}$ and spectral projection-valued measure $E$; a
trial vector is a unit vector $u\in Q(H)$ and its trial value is $q_{H}[u]$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses
of the cited spectral suppliers. Then:

(a) *Trial lower bound.* For every trial vector $u\in Q(H)$,
$$q_{H}[u]\ge E_{0},$$
so every trial value is an upper bound for the model bottom; consequently
$E_{0}=\inf\{q_{H}[u]:u\in Q(H),\ \|u\|=1\}$.

(b) *Gap-overlap control.* Suppose in addition that the bottom is isolated
with gap $g>0$ and let $P:=E(\{E_{0}\})$ (clause (d) of the model). Then for
every trial vector $u$ with $q_{H}[u]\le E_{0}+\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon\ge0$,
$$\bigl\|(I-P)u\bigr\|^{2}\le\frac{\varepsilon}{g};$$
in particular, if $\varepsilon<g$, then $Pu\ne0$.

(c) *Min-max.* Let $\Lambda:=\inf\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H)$ and let
$E_{1}\le E_{2}\le\cdots$ be the discrete eigenvalue ladder of the model
clause (d), with $E_{n}:=\Lambda$ after exhaustion and $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$.
Then for every integer $n\ge1$,
$$E_{n}=\inf_{\substack{L\subseteq Q(H)\ \text{linear}\\ \dim L=n}}\ \sup_{\substack{u\in L\\ \|u\|=1}}q_{H}[u] =\sup_{\substack{F\subseteq Q(H)\ \text{linear}\\ \dim F\le n-1}}\ \inf_{\substack{u\in Q(H)\cap F^{\perp}\\ \|u\|=1}}q_{H}[u],$$
with the infimum over an empty set read as $+\infty$; moreover $E_{1}=E_{0}$,
and when $E_{n}<\Lambda$ both outer values are attained, respectively by a span
of the first $n$ and a span of the first $n-1$ orthonormal eigenvectors.

(d) *Consequence for trial subspaces.* For every linear subspace $L\subseteq
Q(H)$ of dimension $n\ge1$ whose supremum is finite, $E_{n}\le\sup\{q_{H}[u]:
u\in L,\ \|u\|=1\}$; for $n=1$ this is clause (a) with $u$ a unit vector of $L$.

(e) *Reading and scope.* All numbers $E_{0}$, $E_{n}$, $q_{H}[u]$ are read in
joules. For a trial vector in $D(H)$ the trial value is the mean energy of the
pure preparation in the moment reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]]; for a trial vector in
$Q(H)\setminus D(H)$ it is a form value and no outcome-law mean is asserted.
The theorem asserts nothing about whether the infimum in (a) is attained,
about a ground eigenvector, about time evolution, equilibration or
environmental coupling, and about any measured energy; it is a statement about
the declared operator $H$.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.2 printed pages 212-213 (PDF pages 220-221): Rayleigh's theorem, the bound <H> >= E0 and the variational principle with a parameter-dependent trial wavefunction

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 1 'Wave Mechanics', Section 5 printed pages 19-21 (PDF pages 18-20): E_gs <= <H>_psi for a normalised trial wavefunction (5.13) and the functional F[psi] (5.20)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.3 printed pages 117-119 (PDF pages 129-131): the min-max theorem (Theorem 4.10) with the form-domain remark, and Section 4.4 printed pages 119-121 (PDF pages 131-133): eigenspace estimates

items.physical_scope: The variational and min-max statements of the declared trial model: every trial value is at least the model bottom E0, a trial value within epsilon of an isolated bottom with gap g forces ground-projection content at least 1 - epsilon/g, and the model's discrete eigenvalues below the essential spectrum are exactly the min-max values over trial subspaces of the form domain. All quantities are readings of the declared operator; no measurement, apparatus, sampling model or laboratory identification is asserted.

items.title: Nondegenerate stationary perturbation of a simple gapped label: first- and second-order coefficients and an explicit cubic remainder
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] in the
**simple-label case**: $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in
\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ with $v=\|V\|\ge0$, $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on
$D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and $E$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ of
**multiplicity one** with gap at least $g>0$,
$\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let $\psi_{0}$ be a
normalized eigenvector, $P_{0}\psi_{0}=\psi_{0}$, let
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}, \qquad Q_{0}=I-P_{0},$$
be the reduced inverse of the model clause (c)(iii). In the branch $v>0$ put
$$R:=\frac{g}{8v}.$$
Then clauses (a)-(e) hold for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<R$
in this positive-norm branch; clause (f) covers $v=0$ independently of $R$:

(a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; the model's followed label
$E_{\lambda}$ of the contour $|z-E|=g/2$ exists, is the unique spectral value
of $H(\lambda)$ inside that contour, is real, and its spectral projection is
the orthogonal rank-one projection
$P_{\lambda}=E_{H(\lambda)}(\{E_{\lambda}\})$;

(b) the gauge-fixed eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_{\lambda}\psi_{0}}{\langle P_{\lambda}\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle}$$
is analytic in $\lambda$, satisfies $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle=1$
and $(H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)$, and
$$q:=2|\lambda|v/g\le\tfrac14,\qquad \|P_{\lambda}-P_{0}\|\le\tfrac13,\qquad \|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2 ;$$

(c) the model's label identity
$$E_{\lambda}=\bigl\langle (H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\bigr\rangle =E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle$$
holds, so the deviation $\lambda\mapsto E_{\lambda}-E$ of the model's energy
label is controlled by the perturbation alone;

(d) the exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0},\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,$$
with $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^{2}/g$; the
second-order coefficient involves the whole complementary spectral subspace of
$H_{0}$ through $S$, continuum included;

(e) the cubic remainder obeys
$$\left|E_{\lambda}-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^{2}}{2}E''(0)\right| \le \frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^{3}}{1-|\lambda|/R},$$
so at $|\lambda|=R/2$ the bound is $g/32$ and for $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at
most $128v^{3}|\lambda|^{3}/g^{2}$;

(f) if $v=0$, that is $V=0$, then $P_{\lambda}=P_{0}$, $E_{\lambda}=E$ and
$\psi(\lambda)=\psi_{0}$ for every real $\lambda$, and no radius involving
division by $v$ is used in this branch;

(g) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the multiplicity
one of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts no unbounded or
degenerate perturbation theorem, no time-dependent perturbation, and no
statement about which branch of the family a preparation occupies.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1 printed pages 203-205 (PDF pages 211-213): the perturbative expansions (9.2)-(9.11), the first-order shift E_b = <E0|Delta|E0> (9.6) and the second-order shift (9.11), derived under the non-degeneracy assumption

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.6 printed pages 153-159 (PDF pages 165-171): strong and norm resolvent convergence and the analytic perturbation consequences for bounded perturbations

items.physical_scope: The stationary perturbation statement for the declared perturbed-family model with a simple isolated label: self-adjointness of the family for real couplings, existence, uniqueness and reality of the followed label inside the gap contour, the exact first- and second-order energy coefficients with the reduced inverse of the complementary spectral subspace, and the explicit cubic remainder bound on the coupling disk. The theorem concerns spectral data of the declared operator family only; it asserts no ramping protocol, no branch population, no relaxation, no transition rate and no measurement.

items.title: Degenerate stationary perturbation: the perturbed eigenvalues stay within 4 lambda^2 v^2/g of the first-order shifts, and no branch relaxation is asserted
items.statement:
Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] with $H_{0}$
self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$, $v=\|V\|>0$,
$H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on $D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and an isolated
eigenvalue $E$ of $H_{0}$ of **finite multiplicity $r\ge1$** with gap at
least $g>0$,
$\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let
$P_{0}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$, $Q_{0}=I-P_{0}$, and
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
the first-order operator of the model clause (c)(ii). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the
suppliers. Then for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g/4$:

(a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$;

(b) for every real $z$ with $|z-E|+|\lambda|v\le g/2$, the restricted
operator $T_{\lambda}(z):=Q_{0}(H(\lambda)-z)Q_{0}$ on
$Q_{0}D(H_{0})=D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H$ has a bounded two-sided inverse
$B(z):Q_{0}\mathfrak H\to Q_{0}D(H_{0})$ with $\|B(z)\|\le4/g$;

(c) every real eigenvalue $z$ of $H(\lambda)$ with eigenvector $\psi\ne0$
and $|z-E|+|\lambda|v\le g/2$ lies within the first-order shift set:
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(z,\,E+\lambda\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\bigr) \le\frac{4\lambda^{2}v^{2}}{g},$$
where $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the spectrum of the
Hermitian operator $V_{E}$ on the $r$-dimensional eigenspace; moreover
$P_{0}\psi\ne0$ for every such eigenvector. Every eigenvalue in the model's
followed cluster inside $|z-E|<g/2$ lies in this controlled window and
therefore obeys the same bound;

(d) *first-order content.* The eigenvalues of $V_{E}$ are the model's
first-order shifts: the set $E+\lambda\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})$ has at most
$r$ points, all within $|\lambda|v$ of $E$; the entire followed cluster, and every other eigenvalue in the window of (c),
are localised at distance $O(\lambda^{2}v^{2}/g)$ from this set, and no
ordering or one-to-one correspondence between the $r$ spectral branches and
the points of $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})$ is asserted;

(e) *No relaxation or selection.* The theorem is a statement about the
spectra of the declared family. It asserts no instantaneous transition of any
preparation to the branch of the smallest value of
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})$, no relaxation to a lowest branch, no
equilibration and no measurement; which spectral subspace a preparation
occupies is fixed by the preparation and by the evolution postulate P4 of the
declared model, not by the label $E_{\lambda}$;

(f) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the finite
multiplicity of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts nothing about
degenerate essential-spectrum labels, gap-closing families, unbounded
perturbations or time-dependent couplings.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1.2 printed pages 206-208 (PDF pages 214-216): the failure of the non-degenerate expansion at a degenerate level, the diagonalisation of the perturbation eEz within the four-dimensional n=2 subspace and the eigenvalues +/-3eEa0 and 0

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.6 printed pages 153-159 (PDF pages 165-171): resolvent convergence, perturbed spectral projections and the localisation of perturbed eigenvalues for bounded perturbations

items.physical_scope: The degenerate stationary perturbation statement for the declared perturbed-family model with an isolated finite-multiplicity label: self-adjointness of the family, the bounded reduced inverse on the complementary subspace, and the localisation of every perturbed eigenvalue in the controlled gap window within 4 lambda^2 v^2/g of the set of first-order shifts E + lambda spec(P0VP0). The theorem asserts no exact eigenvalue correspondence, no branch ordering, no instantaneous selection of the lowest branch, no relaxation and no measurement.

items.title: WKB approximation on an allowed interval of the declared regime model: explicit Gronwall error bound away from turning points
items.statement:
Adopt the declared WKB regime model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] and let its data
$V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,E,W,\lambda,h$ be as in that model, with
hypothesis (W1) on a closed interval $[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$: $W$ is $C^{2}$
on a neighbourhood of $[a,b]$ and $\lambda-W(\xi)\ge\delta>0$ for some
$\delta>0$ and all $\xi\in[a,b]$. Put
$$p(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0,\qquad \theta(\xi):=\int_{a}^{\xi}p(s)\,ds,\qquad q(\xi):=\frac{3p'(\xi)^{2}}{4p(\xi)^{2}}-\frac{p''(\xi)}{2p(\xi)},$$
and
$$w_{\pm}(\xi):=p(\xi)^{-1/2}e^{\pm i\theta(\xi)/h},\qquad M(\xi):=\begin{pmatrix}w_{+}(\xi)&w_{-}(\xi)\\ w_{+}'(\xi)&w_{-}'(\xi)\end{pmatrix}.$$
Let $u\in C^{2}([a,b];\mathbb C)$ be an exact solution of the dimensionless
model equation $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$ on $[a,b]$, and let
$$c(\xi)=M(\xi)^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}u(\xi)\\ u'(\xi)\end{pmatrix}$$
be its coefficient curve. Then, with $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ the $\ell^{1}$ norm on
$\mathbb C^{2}$ and all quantities read in the model's units:

(a) $\|c(\xi)\|_{1}\le\|c(a)\|_{1}\exp\bigl(h\int_{a}^{\xi}|q(s)|/p(s)\,ds\bigr)$
for every $\xi\in[a,b]$;

(b) $\|c(\xi)-c(a)\|_{1}\le\|c(a)\|_{1}\bigl(\exp\bigl(h\int_{a}^{\xi}|q(s)|/p(s)\,ds\bigr)-1\bigr)$;

(c) *pointwise wavefunction error.* With $\Psi(\xi):=c_{+}(a)w_{+}(\xi)+
c_{-}(a)w_{-}(\xi)$ the leading WKB wave,
$$|u(\xi)-\Psi(\xi)|\le p(\xi)^{-1/2}\|c(a)\|_{1} \Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_{a}^{\xi}\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr);$$

(d) the estimate is exact at each fixed $h$; it degenerates as
$p(\xi)\to0$ and therefore excludes turning points by hypothesis (W1). It
asserts nothing about connecting asymptotics across a turning point, about
barrier transmission or reflection, about packets or detectors, and it makes
no claim that the right-hand side is small unless the dimensionless quantity
$h\int_{a}^{b}|q|/p$ is actually small. The estimate is an error bound of
Gronwall type, not an asymptotic expansion, and the physical reading of the
interval $[a,b]$ is $[x_{a},x_{b}]=\ell[a,b]$ in the line model with potential
$V(\ell\xi)=E_\star W(\xi)$ and energy $E_\star\lambda$.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 5.4 'WKB Approximation' printed and PDF pages 70-72 (the WKB function in the classically allowed region, the amplitude condition and the validity discussion)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 11.6 printed pages 253-254 (PDF pages 261-262): the slowly varying amplitude equation d ln S/dx = -(1/2) d ln k/dx, its integral and the flux-conserving WKBJ wavefunction (11.40)

items.physical_scope: The finite-interval WKB error statement for the declared WKB regime model: on a closed interval on which the dimensionless potential stays strictly below the energy (no turning point), any exact solution of the model equation is compared with its leading WKB wave, with the explicit Gronwall-type error bound of the cited theorem. The statement is exact at each value of the semiclassical parameter; it asserts no asymptotic connection across a turning point, no barrier transmission formula, no wave packet and no measurement.

items.title: Airy connection across a single simple turning point of the declared regime model, with envelope error control
items.statement:
Adopt the declared WKB regime model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] with its data
$V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,W,\lambda,h$, and assume hypothesis (W3) at a
turning point $\xi_{0}$ with $W'(\xi_{0})>0$: on an interval
$[\xi_{0}-r_{0},\xi_{0}+s_{0}]$ with $r_{0},s_{0}>0$ the function
$W-\lambda$ has the single zero $\xi_{0}$, is strictly negative on
$[\xi_{0}-r_{0},\xi_{0})$ (allowed side) and strictly positive on
$(\xi_{0},\xi_{0}+s_{0}]$ (forbidden side). Write, for the two sides,
$$\theta(\xi):=\frac1h\int_{\xi}^{\xi_{0}}\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi')}\,d\xi' \quad(\xi<\xi_{0}),\qquad \Sigma(\xi):=\frac1h\int_{\xi_{0}}^{\xi}\sqrt{W(\xi')-\lambda}\,d\xi' \quad(\xi>\xi_{0}),$$
the nonnegative dimensionless phase and exponent measured from the turning
point into the allowed and forbidden sides. Then there are constants
$0<C_{1}<\infty$ and $C_{0}<\infty$, depending only on
$W,\lambda,\xi_{0},r_{0},s_{0}$ (not on $h$), and $h_0>0$, such that for every $0<h<h_0$:

(a) *Decaying connection.* There is an exact solution $u_{\mathrm{dec}}$ of
the model equation $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$ on
$[\xi_{0}-r_{0},\xi_{0}+s_{0}]$ and a real constant $C\ne0$ with
$$u_{\mathrm{dec}}(\xi)=C\,(W(\xi)-\lambda)^{-1/4} e^{-\Sigma(\xi)}\bigl(1+\delta_{\mathrm{f}}(\xi)\bigr)\qquad(\xi>\xi_{0}),$$
$$u_{\mathrm{dec}}(\xi)=2C\,(\lambda-W(\xi))^{-1/4} \Bigl(\sin\bigl(\theta(\xi)+\tfrac{\pi}{4}\bigr)+\delta_{\mathrm{a}}(\xi)\Bigr) \qquad(\xi<\xi_{0}),$$
where the absolute errors obey, for $\xi\ne\xi_{0}$ away from the turning
point,
$$|\delta_{\mathrm{f}}(\xi)|\le C_{0}\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+h/|\zeta(\xi)|^{3/2}\bigr), \qquad \bigl|\delta_{\mathrm{a}}(\xi)\bigr|\le C_{0}\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+h/|\zeta(\xi)|^{3/2}\bigr),$$
$\zeta$ is the Liouville variable $\zeta(\xi)=\operatorname{sign}
(\xi-\xi_{0})\bigl[\tfrac32\bigl|\int_{\xi_{0}}^{\xi}
\sqrt{|W-\lambda|}\bigr|\bigr]^{2/3}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-liouville-turning-point-transformation]], and
$\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$;

(b) *Growing connection.* There is a second exact solution
$u_{\mathrm{grow}}$, linearly independent of $u_{\mathrm{dec}}$, with
$$u_{\mathrm{grow}}(\xi)=C'\,(W(\xi)-\lambda)^{-1/4} e^{+\Sigma(\xi)}\bigl(1+\delta_{\mathrm{f}}'(\xi)\bigr)\qquad(\xi>\xi_{0}),$$
$$u_{\mathrm{grow}}(\xi)=C'\,(\lambda-W(\xi))^{-1/4} \Bigl(\cos\bigl(\theta(\xi)+\tfrac{\pi}{4}\bigr)+\delta_{\mathrm{a}}'(\xi)\Bigr) \qquad(\xi<\xi_{0}),$$
for a real constant $C'\ne0$, with absolute errors bounded as in (a);

(c) *Derivative and envelope control.* The derivatives
$u_{\mathrm{dec}}',u_{\mathrm{grow}}'$ obey the corresponding bounds with the
derivative envelope $d_{h}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stable-weighted-airy-volterra-connection]] in
place of the value envelope $e_{h}$, so the displayed statements control the
solutions in value and slope;

(d) *Content of the connection.* The factors $2$ in the decaying allowed-side
form of (a) and $1$ in the growing allowed-side form of (b) are the amplitude
relations of the exact Airy pair: the forbidden-side data determine the
constants $C$ and $C'$, and the allowed-side oscillations are the sine and
cosine forms with phase $\pi/4$ measured from the turning point into the
allowed region. The statement excludes rectangular walls, coalescing or
multiple turning points, multi-turn resonances and barrier-top uniformity; it
asserts no transmission or reflection coefficient (that is a separate
statement requiring hypothesis (W2)), no wave packet, no detector and no
measured value; the errors are absolute and blow up as the turning point is
approached, as displayed by the $h/|\zeta|^{3/2}$ term.

items.title: Separated smooth-barrier tunnelling: the declared transmission coefficient is exp(-2S/h) up to explicit small-h and barrier-thickness errors
items.statement:
Adopt the declared WKB regime model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] with its data
$V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,W,\lambda,h$ and assume hypothesis (W2): $W-\lambda$
has exactly two zeros $\xi_{a}<\xi_{b}$ on $\mathbb R$, both simple, is
strictly positive on $(\xi_{a},\xi_{b})$ and strictly negative on
$\mathbb R\setminus[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$. Put
$$S:=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi>0,$$
and let $T(h)$ be the model's declared transmission coefficient of its
clause (d). Then there are $h_0>0$, an $\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$ for $0<h<h_0$, and a constant
$0\le C_{0}<\infty$, both depending only on the model's barrier data
$(W,\lambda,\ell,E_\star)$ and the fixed matching sections, such that
$$\Bigl|T(h)\,e^{2S/h}-1\Bigr|\le \frac{C_{0}\bigl[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}\bigr]} {1-C_{0}\bigl[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}\bigr]}$$
whenever the denominator is positive; consequently
$$T(h)=e^{-2S/h}\Bigl(1+O\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}\bigr)\Bigr).$$
In the physical variables of the line model, where
$V(\ell\xi)=E_\star W(\xi)$ and $E=E_\star\lambda$, one has by
[[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] clause (b)
$$\frac{S}{h}=\frac1\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m\bigl(V(x)-E\bigr)}\,dx, \qquad x_{a}=\ell\xi_{a},\ x_{b}=\ell\xi_{b},$$
so the displayed leading factor is $e^{-2S/h}
=\exp\bigl(-\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V-E)}\,dx\bigr)$,
the exponential of minus twice the classical action integral of the forbidden
region in units of $\hbar$. The statement is conditional on the fixed
compactly supported $C^{5}$ barrier with two separated simple turning points;
rectangular walls, coalescing turning points, barrier-top uniformity and
resonant multiwell interference are excluded, and $T(h)$ is the declared
scattering-current ratio of the model, not a detector response or a measured count; no
wave packet, preparation, apparatus or sampling model is asserted. In
particular, for each fixed barrier,
$$\lim_{h\downarrow0}T(h)\,e^{2S/h}=1 .$$

Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Sections 5.3-5.6 printed and PDF pages 64-75: 5.3 Square Potential Barrier p. 64, 5.4 WKB Approximation p. 70, 5.5 Cold Emission p. 72, 5.6 Alpha Decay p. 73 (barrier penetration and the WKB tunnelling exponent)

F. W. J. Olver, Asymptotics and Special Functions (1974), Chapter 11 (connection formulas and barrier penetration for second-order equations with two turning points; standard monograph), consulted through the NIST DLMF Airy survey

items.physical_scope: The separated smooth-barrier transmission statement for the declared WKB regime model: the declared transmission coefficient equals the exponential of minus twice the barrier WKB exponent per unit h, with the quantitative small-h and exponentially small correction bound of the cited theorem, and the physical exponent is (1/hbar) times the classical action integral over the forbidden region. The statement is conditional on a fixed compactly supported C^5 barrier with exactly two separated simple turning points; it excludes rectangular walls, coalescing turning points, barrier-top uniformity and resonant multiwell interference, and it asserts no detector, wave packet or measured transmission.

items.title: What the controlled-approximations page adopts, proves and does not claim: gaps, branch populations, turning points and the static-Stark limitation
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Adopted model clauses.** The page declares three models: the variational
  trial model [[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-variational-trial-model]]
  (a self-adjoint energy observable bounded below, its form domain and trial
  value), the perturbed family
  [[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] (a bounded
  self-adjoint perturbation of a gapped isolated label) and the WKB regime
  model [[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] (the
  nondimensionalised one-dimensional stationary equation with a declared
  semiclassical parameter and a compactly supported $C^{5}$ potential), plus
  the static finite-level dipole coupling
  [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]]. Each
  declaration is a model assumption; none is derived from P1-P7.

- **What is proved.** Conditional on those declarations the page proves: the
  trial lower bound, the gap-overlap control and the min-max characterisation
  of the discrete ladder
  ([[pthm-nrqm-approximations-variational-bounds-and-min-max]]); the
  nondegenerate perturbation expansion with explicit cubic remainder
  ([[pthm-nrqm-approximations-nondegenerate-perturbation-expansion]]); the
  degenerate first-order splitting localisation within
  $4\lambda^{2}v^{2}/g$
  ([[pthm-nrqm-approximations-degenerate-first-order-splitting]]); the
  allowed-region WKB Gronwall error
  ([[pthm-nrqm-approximations-wkb-allowed-region-error]]); the single
  simple-turning-point Airy connection with envelope errors
  ([[pthm-nrqm-approximations-turning-point-connection]]); and the separated
  smooth-barrier transmission asymptotics
  ([[pthm-nrqm-approximations-barrier-transmission-asymptotics]]). Every one
  of these statements carries its hypotheses explicitly: the gap $g>0$, the
  boundedness of the perturbation, the smoothness of $W$, the separation of
  the turning points, and the value of the semiclassical parameter.

- **No attained ground state is assumed.** The variational statements use the
  form domain $Q(H)$ and the declared spectral lower bound; they do not
  assume that the bottom $E_{0}$ is an eigenvalue, that a ground eigenvector
  exists, or that the trial infimum is attained. The gap-overlap clause is
  the only place where an isolated bottom is used, and it states exactly the
  overlap forced by a trial value within $\varepsilon$ of the bottom.

- **No branch population or equilibration.** The perturbation theorems locate
  spectral labels of the declared families; they assert no instantaneous
  transition of a preparation to the branch with the smallest first-order
  shift, no relaxation to a lowest branch and no equilibration. The
  motivating textbook conjecture of a jump to the lowest branch is not
  imported: for a closed system, which spectral subspace a preparation
  occupies is fixed by the preparation and by the evolution of P4
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); an equilibration statement
  would require a separately declared environment or dissipation model, which
  this page does not supply.

- **Turning points and barriers.** The allowed-region error excludes turning
  points by hypothesis; the connection theorem treats a single simple
  turning point and does not produce a transmission coefficient; the barrier
  theorem assumes exactly two separated simple turning points of a compactly
  supported $C^{5}$ barrier and excludes rectangular walls, coalescing
  turning points, barrier-top uniformity and resonant multiwell interference.
  The declared transmission coefficient is a matching datum of the model, not
  a detector response.

- **The static-Stark limitation.** The uncompressed static perturbation of a
  Coulomb model by a uniform field is the unbounded multiplication term
  $-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D$; the energy form of $H_{\kappa}$ plus
  that term has no lower bound when the field is nonzero (translating a
  fixed normalized compactly supported smooth relative-state trial function
  along $-t\mathbf E_{\rm ext}$ lowers the linear term $q\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot r$
  by $-tq|\mathbf E_{\rm ext}|^2$; its kinetic form stays constant and its
  Coulomb form tends to zero, so the trial energy tends to $-\infty$), so no bounded-perturbation theorem of this page applies to
  it. This page therefore covers only the compressed finite-level operator of
  [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]], and it
  states no eigenvalue theorem for the uncompressed model.

- **Empirical status.** No experiment, reported observation, measured shift,
  splitting, transmission or count appears on this page; no apparatus,
  calibration, sampling or uncertainty record is supplied. The statements are
  conditional predictions of the declared models. A comparison with data
  would test the combined assumptions -- preparation, isolation, parameter
  identification, truncation, field description and detection response --
  under the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); agreement would be
  evidence about that combination, not a deductive proof of the model, and a
  discrepancy would require the auxiliary assumptions to be examined before
  the model is rejected.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1.2 printed pages 206-208 (PDF pages 214-216): the degenerate-subspace diagonalisation of the perturbation, together with the conjecture that the system 'jumps' to the lowest branch, which is not imported as a deduction

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.3 printed pages 117-119 (PDF pages 129-131) and Section 6.6 printed pages 153-159 (PDF pages 165-171): the min-max theorem and the bounded-perturbation resolvent estimates on which the page's conditional statements rest

items.physical_scope: A scope and status record for the controlled-approximations page: the adopted model clauses, the proved conditional statements with their gap, smoothness and boundedness hypotheses, the explicit exclusions (equilibration and branch selection, unbounded and static-field perturbations, rectangular and coalescing turning-point configurations, detectors and measurements), and the absence of any empirical record on this page.

items.title: A two-level finite-gap model: exact eigenvalues, the second-order correction and a finite check of the cubic remainder bound
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 for a declared **two-level system**
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) with state space
$\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{2}$ in the standard orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$
and with the observable reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; read all
energies in joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Fix
real **gap** and **coupling** parameters $g>0$ and $c>0$, and declare the
model's energy observable family by the perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] with
$$H_{0}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&g\end{pmatrix},\qquad V:=\begin{pmatrix}0&c\\c&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V\quad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).$$
Then $H_{0}$ has the isolated simple eigenvalue $E=0$ with gap $g$,
$v=\|V\|=c$, $\psi_{0}=e_{1}$, and the reduced inverse of the model clause
(c)(iii) is $S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1/g)$ on $Q_{0}\mathfrak H=\mathbb
Ce_{2}$. Then:

(a) for every real $\lambda$ the matrix $H(\lambda)$ is Hermitian with exactly
two eigenvalues
$$E_{\pm}(\lambda)=\frac{g\pm\sqrt{g^{2}+4\lambda^{2}c^{2}}}{2},$$
both simple for $\lambda\ne0$ and spanning the spectrum for every $\lambda$;
in the model's valid contour range $2|\lambda|c/g<1$, its distinguished
label is $E_{\lambda}=E_{-}(\lambda)$. The formula $E_-$ remains an exact
continuous lower spectral branch for all real couplings, even beyond that
fixed-contour range;

(b) the exact perturbation coefficients are
$$E'(0)=0,\qquad E''(0)=-\frac{2c^{2}}{g},\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0}=-\frac{c}{g}e_{2},\qquad \psi_{0}=e_{1},$$
and the exact eigenvalue has the convergent expansion
$$E_{-}(\lambda)=-\frac{\lambda^{2}c^{2}}{g} +\frac{\lambda^{4}c^{4}}{g^{3}}-\frac{2\lambda^{6}c^{6}}{g^{5}}+O(\lambda^{8});$$

(c) the cubic remainder bound of
[[pthm-nrqm-approximations-nondegenerate-perturbation-expansion]] clause (e)
holds in this model for every $|\lambda|<R=g/(8c)$, and at the test point
$\lambda=R/2=g/(16c)$ the exact remainder and its bound are
$$E_{-}\!\left(\frac{g}{16c}\right)+\frac{g}{256} =\frac{g}{2}\Bigl(1-\frac{\sqrt{65}}{8}\Bigr)+\frac{g}{256}\approx1.51\cdot10^{-5}g \le\frac{g}{32},$$
so the finite check is satisfied with a wide margin;

(d) the exact spectrum computed in (a) is a spectral statement about the
declared two-level family; it identifies no physical system, asserts no
measured splitting, and asserts nothing about which of the two spectral
subspaces a preparation occupies (that is fixed by the preparation and the
evolution of P4, not by the perturbative expansion).

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1 printed pages 203-205 (PDF pages 211-213): the perturbative expansion, the first-order coefficient (9.6) and the second-order coefficient (9.11) for a non-degenerate level

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Section 5 'Ammonia molecule in an electric field' printed and PDF pages 11-16: the exactly solvable two-state Stark family with eigenvalues E0 +/- sqrt(mu^2 E^2 + Delta^2), the closed analogue of the check performed here

items.physical_scope: A conditional two-level computation inside the declared perturbed-family model with a finite gap: the exact eigenvalues of the family, its second-order coefficient, the exact quartic expansion, and a finite numerical check of the page's cubic remainder bound at half the perturbation radius. The example is a model computation in the declared finite-dimensional subspace; it asserts no physical system identification, no measured splitting and no transition.

items.title: A finite-level static Stark model: vanishing first-order shift, exact quadratic splitting and a finite check of the remainder bound
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 for the declared two-body Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d), in the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the dipole
operator $D_{j}=-qQ_{j}$ and the compressed finite-level coupling of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]]. Use
the Coulomb mass parameter $m=\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$ and
$a_{\mu}:=\hbar^{2}/(\mu\kappa)>0$. Choose as
the finite-level subspace the **declared two-dimensional subspace**
$$W:=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
where $\psi_{1}$ and $\psi_{2}$ are normalized bound states of the model with
angular labels $(n,l,m)=(1,0,0)$ and $(2,1,0)$ supplied by
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], so that
$H_{\kappa}\psi_{1}=E_{1}\psi_{1}$, $H_{\kappa}\psi_{2}=E_{2}\psi_{2}$ with
$$E_{1}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},\qquad E_{2}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{8\hbar^{2}},\qquad \Delta:=E_{2}-E_{1}=\frac{3m\kappa^{2}}{8\hbar^{2}}>0 .$$
Choose the external field along the third axis of the declared frame,
$\mathbf E_{\rm ext}=(0,0,\mathcal E)$ with $\mathcal E>0$ in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, and use the dimensionless coupling
$$\lambda:=\frac{\mathcal E}{1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}},\qquad V:=-(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})\,D^{W}_{3},$$
so that the Stark model of the postulate reads
$$H_{S}(\mathcal E)=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad H_{0}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&0\\0&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}$$
in the declared orthonormal basis. Then:

(a) the compression of the dipole matrix has the form
$$D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0,\qquad D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad D_{\rm rel}:=|\langle\psi_{2},D_{3}\psi_{1}\rangle|>0,$$
with unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$, where the phase of $\psi_{2}$ is chosen to make
the off-diagonal entry positive. The local computation below gives
$D_{\rm rel}=128\sqrt2\,q a_{\mu}/243>0$ from the declared model parameters;
this is an exact model identity, with no measured value of any parameter.
The diagonal entries vanish by angular degree selection, and only $Q_{0}$
can contribute between the chosen $m=0$ states; nonvanishing is proved by
explicit radial and angular integration;

(b) $v=\|V\|=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})$ in joules and the family
$H_{S}$ has the exact eigenvalues
$$F_{\pm}(\mathcal E)=\frac{E_{1}+E_{2}}{2} \pm\sqrt{\Bigl(\frac{\Delta}{2}\Bigr)^{2}+\bigl(D_{\rm rel}\mathcal E\bigr)^{2}},$$
the lower branch $F_{-}$ being the model's followed label for
dimensionless couplings $0\le\lambda<R:=\Delta/(8v)$, equivalently
$0\le\mathcal E<\Delta/(8D_{\rm rel})$, with $\Delta$ playing the role of the gap $g$;

(c) the page's perturbation theorem applies with nondegenerate label
$E_{1}$ (gap $\Delta$), and gives the vanishing first-order shift
$$E'(0)=0$$
and the exact second-order coefficient
$$E''(0)=-\frac{2D_{\rm rel}^{2}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})^{2}}{\Delta},$$
equivalently the quadratic Stark shift
$$F_{-}(\mathcal E)=E_{1}-\frac{D_{\rm rel}^{2}\mathcal E^{2}}{\Delta} +O(\mathcal E^{4});$$

(d) the finite remainder check at half the perturbation radius
$\lambda=R/2$, equivalently $\mathcal E=\Delta/(16D_{\rm rel})$, gives the exact remainder
$$\Bigl|F_{-}+\frac{\Delta}{256}-E_{1}\Bigr|=\Delta\,\frac{129-16\sqrt{65}}{256}=\frac{\Delta}{256(129+16\sqrt{65})}<\frac{\Delta}{32768}<\frac{\Delta}{32},$$
so the page's cubic bound is satisfied at this coupling with a wide margin;

(e) scope: the computation is conditional on the declared truncated
two-state model and the adopted coupling; it identifies no laboratory atom,
reports no measured shift and no polarizability value, asserts no transition
rate, and does not treat the uncompressed linear potential
$-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D$. The postulate excludes that model and
proves its common-test-domain expectations unbounded below for every nonzero
uniform field; no full energy-form domain is used here.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1.1 printed pages 205-206 (PDF pages 213-214): the quadratic Stark effect of the hydrogen ground state, Eb = eE<100|z|100> = 0 by parity and the second-order formula (9.16)-(9.17); and Section 9.1.2 printed pages 206-208 (PDF pages 214-216): the linear Stark effect from the diagonalisation of eEz within the degenerate n=2 subspace

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Section 5 'Ammonia molecule in an electric field' printed and PDF pages 11-16: the two-state ammonia Stark family H = E0 I - Delta sigma1 + muE sigma3 and its exact eigenvalues E0 +/- sqrt(mu^2E^2 + Delta^2), the exact template for the closed form used here

items.physical_scope: A conditional finite-level computation in the declared two-body Coulomb model with the adopted static finite-level dipole coupling: the compressed two-state Stark family built from the model's 1s-like and 2p-like relative states, the vanishing diagonal dipole matrix elements by the angular selection rule, the exact closed-form eigenvalues of the two-state family, the vanishing first-order and the exact second-order coefficient of the page's non-degenerate theorem, and a finite numeric check of the cubic remainder bound. The example identifies no laboratory atom, asserts no measured Stark shift or polarizability value, and states no transition or lifetime; the uncompressed linear-potential model is explicitly outside its scope.

items.title: A spin-one multiplet in a uniform field: the exact Zeeman spectrum and degenerate first-order check
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P6 for the massive spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), together with the
effective magnetic-moment coupling
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with real
gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma:=\gamma_{1}$ and the spin-one internal factor
$\mathbb C^{3}$ with spin operators $S_{1},S_{2},S_{3}$; read energies in
joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Declare the
**finite-level Zeeman model** by the perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] with
$$\mathfrak H:=\mathbb C^{3},\qquad H_{0}:=\varepsilon I_{3},\qquad V:=-\gamma B_{z}S_{3},$$
where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ is a declared multiplet energy, $B_{z}>0$ is
the field magnitude in tesla of the uniform field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$,
so that the family is $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ with real coupling
$\lambda$ (dimensionless, equal to $1$ for the physical field) and
$v=\|V\|=|\gamma|B_{z}\hbar$. For the physical value $\lambda=1$ the family is
the model's Zeeman operator on the internal multiplet. Then:

(a) the perturbation preserves the multiplet: $[H_{0},V]=0$, the
first-order operator is $V_{E}=V$, and its eigenvalues counted with
multiplicity are $-\hbar\gamma B_{z},0,+\hbar\gamma B_{z}$ in joules. If
$\gamma\ne0$, these are three distinct simple eigenvalues; if $\gamma=0$,
the only eigenvalue is $0$ with multiplicity three. Thus the first-order
operator describes a triply degenerate level when the adopted magnetic
coupling vanishes;

(b) the exact energy eigenvalues of the family, counted with multiplicity,
are
$$\varepsilon-\lambda\hbar\gamma B_{z},\qquad \varepsilon,\qquad \varepsilon+\lambda\hbar\gamma B_{z}.$$
They are three distinct simple levels exactly when $\lambda\gamma\ne0$;
when $\lambda=0$ or $\gamma=0$, the only energy is $\varepsilon$ with
multiplicity three. Each eigenvalue is affine in $\lambda$, so its
second-order and higher Taylor coefficients vanish identically;

(c) when $v>0$, the page's degenerate theorem applies for every $g>0$ (the
gap condition is vacuous because the spectrum of $H_{0}$ is the single value
$\varepsilon$) and every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g/4$; each
eigenvalue $z$ then satisfies
$\operatorname{dist}(z,\varepsilon+\lambda\operatorname{spec}(V_{E}))
\le 4\lambda^{2}v^{2}/g$, and the exact spectrum in (b) shows that this
distance is $0$. If $v=0$, equivalently $\gamma=0$, then
$H(\lambda)=\varepsilon I_{3}$ for every real $\lambda$, so the same
distance is $0$ directly, without invoking the theorem's positive-norm
hypothesis. In both cases the first-order eigenvalue set is exact, with
multiplicity retained as in (a)-(b);

(d) the model's conserved component and transverse precession are those of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] for the declared field:
the component $S_{3}$ is conserved along the flow of $H(\lambda)$ and the
transverse spin means precess at the Larmor angular signed frequency $\lambda\gamma B_{z}$, equal to $\gamma B_z$ at the physical coupling $\lambda=1$;

(e) no branch selection: the energy eigenspaces of (b) are spectral data of
the family; a preparation in any eigenstate is stationary, and a superposition
evolves with the relative phases of (b). The example asserts
no instantaneous transition of any preparation to the lowest sublevel, no
relaxation and no measurement; which sublevel a preparation occupies is
fixed by the preparation and by P4.

items.title: Tunnelling asymptotic limits: the smooth-barrier semiclassical limit and the exact rectangular prefactor comparison
items.statement:
Adopt the declared one-dimensional line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] and the WKB regime model
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] with their framework
postulates
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]),
with units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *Smooth-barrier semiclassical limit.* Let $V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,E,W,
\lambda,h$ be data of the WKB regime model satisfying its hypothesis (W2),
with exponent $S=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W-\lambda}\,d\xi$ and declared
transmission coefficient $T(h)$. Then there are $\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$
and $C_{0}<\infty$, depending only on the barrier data, such that
$$\Bigl|T(h)e^{2S/h}-1\Bigr| \le\frac{C_{0}[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}]}{1-C_{0}[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}]}$$
whenever the denominator is positive; in particular
$$\lim_{h\downarrow0}T(h)e^{2S/h}=1,$$
and the physical reading of the limit is the exponential law
$T\approx\exp\bigl(-\frac2\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V-E)}\,dx\bigr)$
with prefactor tending to one;

(b) *Rectangular thick-barrier limit.* For the **rectangular wall model**
excluded by the smooth theorem, take the exact scattering solution of the
line model with $V(x)=U$ for $0<x<a$ and $V=0$ otherwise, $U>E>0$,
$k=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar$, $\kappa=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar$ and exact transmission
$$T_{\rm rect}=\Bigl[1+\frac{U^{2}\sinh^{2}(\kappa a)}{4E(U-E)}\Bigr]^{-1};$$
then, as $\kappa a\to\infty$,
$$\frac{T_{\rm rect}}{e^{-2\kappa a}}\longrightarrow \frac{16E(U-E)}{U^{2}}=\frac{16k^{2}\kappa^{2}}{(k^{2}+\kappa^{2})^{2}},$$
so in the rectangular model the exponential law holds with the profile-dependent
prefactor $16E(U-E)/U^{2}$; the exponent $2\kappa a$ equals the classical
WKB exponent $2B/\hbar$ of the rectangular barrier, and the limit shows that
the exponential alone does not determine the prefactor;

(c) *Reading of the comparison.* Statement (a) is a theorem about smooth
compactly supported barriers with separated simple turning points, and its
prefactor-one conclusion uses the Airy matching of that class; statement (b)
is an exact model computation for a piecewise constant wall, whose sharp
discontinuities are precisely why it is excluded from (a). Neither statement
asserts a measured transmission, a detector response, a wave packet or an
apparatus; both are conditional statements about the declared
one-dimensional models.

items.physical_scope: Two asymptotic statements about declared one-dimensional barrier transmission data: the semiclassical limit of the smooth compactly supported barrier of the WKB regime model, in which the ratio of the declared transmission coefficient to exp(-2S/h) tends to one; and the exact thick-barrier limit of the rectangular wall model, whose profile-dependent limit prefactor is 16E(U-E)/U^2 and can differ from one, showing that the exponential law alone does not determine the prefactor and that rectangular walls are outside the smooth-barrier theorem. No measured transmission, detector, sample or apparatus is asserted.

items.title: What the controlled-approximations examples establish and what they do not
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Four conditional computations of the declared
  models of the companion A page: the exact two-level finite-gap family with
  its second-order coefficient and a finite check of the cubic remainder
  bound
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-two-level-finite-gap-correction]]); the finite
  level static Stark model of the declared Coulomb pair with vanishing
  first-order shift, the exact quadratic splitting and a finite check of the
  remainder bound
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-stark-finite-level-shift]]); the spin-one
  multiplet in a uniform field with the exact linear splitting and the
  degenerate first-order check
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-zeeman-multiplet-splitting]]); and the two
  tunnelling asymptotic limits, the smooth-barrier semiclassical limit and
  the exact rectangular thick-barrier prefactor
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-smooth-barrier-tunnelling-limits]]). Each
  computation states its model and its sources and cites the page's theorem
  it checks.

- **What the checks are.** The first two examples verify the quantitative
  remainder bound of
  [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-nondegenerate-perturbation-expansion]] on
  exactly solvable two-state families, one with a finite gap and a
  second-order shift, one with the compressed dipole coupling of
  [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]]; the
  third verifies the first-order localisation of
  [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-degenerate-first-order-splitting]] in the
  exactly diagonalizable Zeeman family; the fourth compares two asymptotic
  limits, one covered by
  [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-barrier-transmission-asymptotics]] and one
  explicitly excluded by it. These are mathematical checks inside declared
  models, not tests of the models against data.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no measured Stark or
  Zeeman shift, no splitting value, no gyromagnetic ratio, no measured matrix element
  or polarizability value, no transmission count, no detector response, no
  apparatus, no calibration, no sampling model and no uncertainty record
  appears; the radial dipole parameter $D_{\rm rel}$ of the Stark example is
  computed exactly from the declared charge and Coulomb length scale,
  and is not measured. The examples
  assert no transition rate, no lifetime and no branch-relaxation process;
  see [[rem-nrqm-approximations-scope-and-empirical-status]] for the
  corresponding scope record of the A page.

- **Deferred content.** Empirical numerical matrix-element comparisons for concrete Coulomb
  systems, time-dependent driving, transition rates, adiabatic evolution, and
  any comparison with measured spectra belong to the driven-dynamics and
  light-matter pairs of the track; the uncompressed static-field model is
  outside the present scope by the postulate's exclusion clause.
